name_en: Igisu Dofu — a jellied summer dish of seaweed and soybean flour set like agar
summary_ja: 海藻のいぎすと生の大豆粉をだし汁で煮溶かし、寒天のように冷やし固める今治の料理。ひんやりとした食感で暑い盛りの食欲をそそり、エビなどの具を入れる家と入れない家で味わいが分かれるという。
summary_en: Igisu seaweed and raw soybean flour are simmered into stock and chilled firm like agar, a dish from Imabari. Its cool texture is meant to coax back a summer appetite, and households differ over whether to fold in shrimp or leave it plain.
source_title: いぎす豆腐 愛媛県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Izumiya — a scattered sushi made with seasoned soybean pulp instead of rice
summary_ja: 酢飯の代わりに味付けしたおからを使う卯の花ずし。別子銅山を開いた住友家の屋号「泉屋」に由来すると伝わり、米を食べにくかった庶民が見た目だけでも真似た料理という。宇和島では丸ずしと呼ぶ。
summary_en: A scattered-sushi variant that uses seasoned soybean pulp (okara) in place of vinegared rice. It's said to take its name from Izumiya, the trade name of the Sumitomo family who opened the Besshi copper mine, after commoners who couldn't easily afford rice mimicked the look of their sushi. In Uwajima it's called maru-zushi.
source_title: いずみや 愛媛県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Fukumen — flaked white fish over konjac noodles, colored to mark the four seasons
summary_ja: 白身魚をほぐして甘辛く煮たそぼろを、麺状に切ったこんにゃくにまぶす宇和島の行事食。ピンクは春、緑は夏、みかん色は秋、白は冬と四季を色で表すとされ、婚礼や長寿祝いに供される。
summary_en: Flaked white fish, simmered sweet and salty, is worked into thin-cut strands of konjac styled like noodles — a festival dish from Uwajima. The colors are said to stand for the seasons, pink for spring through white for winter, and it's served at weddings and longevity celebrations.
source_title: ふくめん 愛媛県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
